misconception.text: Current is used up as it goes round a circuit.

correction.text: The same current flows at every point of a series circuit. What is used up is the energy, not the current.

signal.text: Our own teaching of the section, waiting for a paper question that shows the same mistake.

misconception.text: Putting a resistor in a series circuit changes the current everywhere.

correction.text: It does, and that is why a series resistor dims the whole circuit rather than one lamp.

signal.text: Our own teaching of the section, waiting for a paper question that shows the same mistake.

misconception.text: Current flows through a thicker wire faster.

correction.text: Current is the rate of flow of charge. A thicker wire is a smaller resistance, so more charge passes each second.

signal.text: Our own teaching of the section, waiting for a paper question that shows the same mistake.

misconception.text: The resistance of a wire depends on its length.

correction.text: It depends on the length, the cross section, and the material, and it rises with temperature for most metals.

signal.text: Our own teaching of the section, waiting for a paper question that shows the same mistake.

stem.text: A cell of emf $12\,\text{V}$ and internal resistance $0.5\,\Omega$ supplies a current of $4\,\text{A}$. The terminal voltage is

explanation.text: The terminal voltage is the emf less the drop across the internal resistance: $V = \mathcal{E} - Ir = 12 - (4)(0.5) = 10\,\text{V}$.

stem.text: Kirchhoff's junction rule is a statement of the conservation of

explanation.text: The sum of the currents entering a junction equals the sum leaving it, because charge is conserved.

stem.text: In a null measurement method, the galvanometer reads zero because

options.text: no current flows through the galvanometer

explanation.text: The bridge is balanced, so the potential difference across the galvanometer is zero and no current flows through it.

stem.text: The resistance of a uniform wire is halved when its length is halved. This is because resistance is

options.text: directly proportional to the square of the length

explanation.text: For a uniform wire $R = \rho\frac{L}{A}$, so halving the length halves the resistance.

stem.text: The main advantage of alternating current over direct current for power distribution is that

options.text: AC can be stepped up and down by a transformer
AC does not produce a magnetic field
AC dissipates less power in the wires

explanation.text: A transformer works only on alternating current, so AC can be raised to a high voltage for transmission and lowered again for use.
